prize_parts.citation: for the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand cleavage
for the conception and demonstration of heterobifunctional degraders that induce targeted protein degradation

statement.case_for: Both parts turn a biological process into a defined chemical reaction and hand biologists a general tool. Base editing is deaminase chemistry on a single nucleobase, delivered by a programmable scaffold, and it has been reproduced in many laboratories and organisms and is now in clinical use. Induced-proximity degradation reframes drug action as event-driven chemistry: a small molecule forces a ubiquitin ligase onto a target, and the mechanism can be measured, for example as degradation kinetics and ternary-complex formation. Pairing them gives a coherent prize on chemical control of the genome and of the proteome. It also keeps the total at three people, and both attributions can be defended. Liu is the conceptual driver of base editing, while Crews and Deshaies founded the PROTAC concept. These two were ranked in the top three by four and five of the eight members respectively in the openings, so the pairing draws on the broadest support in the room rather than on my own first place.
statement.case_against: Base editing may be read as a refinement of the 2020 CRISPR prize, and the long-term safety record (bystander edits, RNA off-target deamination) is still short. For PROTACs no approved drug exists yet, so the therapeutic payoff is unproven, and a Crews/Deshaies citation leaves out Handa and Ito (cereblon and the thalidomide glue mechanism) and Ciulli (structure-guided VHL ligands). Dropping Komor and Gaudelli to fit three names is also a real cost, because they made the cytosine and adenine editors, and attribution inside the Liu laboratory is a judgement call. Finally, two chemical-biology-for-medicine themes in one prize may look like a narrow selection from a field that spans many other areas.

responses.point: Aili ranks ionizable lipid nanoparticles first: pKa-tuned lipids are the enabling delivery chemistry for siRNA drugs and the mRNA vaccines, validated at global scale and not yet recognised after the 2023 Medicine prize. Aili also proposes Liu alone for base editing.
responses.response: I agree that the chemical principle is clear and the clinical proof is unequivocal, and I ranked it fourth. My reservation is attribution. Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer all have decisive claims, and some key lipid chemistry was done in industry, so any three names would be hard to defend. The 2023 Medicine citation on nucleoside modification also covers the same therapeutic story. I would keep it as a first alternative, but not ahead of two parts whose credit is clearer. I welcome your support for Liu alone and take it as a basis for the trimmed laureate list.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks long-range electron transfer through proteins first as an overdue, quantitatively tested physical basis of respiration, and he proposes Liu alone for base editing and Crews and Deshaies for the degrader concept, with Handa for the glue strand.
responses.response: Your electron-transfer case is the most mature on the list and I take the physical-chemistry argument seriously. Marcus theory was recognised in 1992, so I would want a clear statement of what the Gray/Winkler experiments add beyond it. On degraders I accept your split of the concept. I have left Handa out of my three only because of the cap on names, and I would be open to a Crews/Deshaies/Handa configuration if the committee prefers a glue strand. That would need base editing to be dropped or a single-part prize, because the union cannot exceed three people.

responses.point: Sparr ranks biomolecular phase separation first as a new organising principle of the cell, grounded in multivalency and polymer physics, with the Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen core.
responses.response: The concept is influential and I do not dispute its originality. As someone who measures things in cells, I am cautious about maturity. Whether many condensates are truly phase separated in vivo, at physiological concentrations, remains disputed, and Linke makes a similar point in his own ranking. A measured read-out of function is still missing for many cited examples. I would hold it as an alternative rather than in the prize this year, and I would ask whether the committee wants the citation to rest on in vitro reconstitution or on cellular function.

responses.point: Linke ranks halide perovskite solar absorbers first, citing a rise from about 4 percent to over 25 percent efficiency, strong independent confirmation, and a clear physical story, with stability and lead toxicity as the caveats.
responses.response: The efficiency record and the replication are not in doubt. My concern is that the credit is among six names and the cell was first made as a sensitised device before the solid-state step, so the three-name cut (Miyasaka, Snaith, Park) leaves out Grätzel, Kanatzidis and Seok. I also ask whether stability under operation, which is a measurement question, is settled enough for a citation about an absorber discovery, or whether it is a materials-engineering issue the discovery itself does not address.

uncertainties: Whether the committee would accept two separate chemical-biology achievements in one prize, or would prefer a single-part prize.
Whether Crews and Deshaies alone is a fair credit for PROTACs without Handa and Ito for the glue mechanism, and without Ciulli.
Whether base editing is judged sufficiently distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Whether Komor and Gaudelli should be named alongside Liu, which would remove room for a second part.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. My work on dNTP pools and ribonucleotide reductase is adjacent to nucleic-acid chemistry in base editing but I have no collaboration or institutional tie to any shortlisted candidate. I will watch for ties to the ubiquitin-ligase field.
